feature.summary: Sorting exists: on web, desktop-hosted web and mobile, clicking a column header sorts the shown rows, ascending, descending, then back. Filtering and Excel-style tables with header, banding and a name are not built. The workbook writer writes no table or filter parts.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person order the rows of a table or workbook sheet in the chat preview by one column. Filtering and table objects are not available.
purpose.why_it_exists: People scan results by value, for example largest first. The brief also lists tables and filters (S29.09, S29.10) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/029-spreadsheet-and-data-analysis-workspace.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone reading a table or workbook in chat.
problems_solved: Find the biggest or smallest values quickly.
Numbers sort by value, not as text (tabular.ts:88-105).
use_cases: Sort a sales table by revenue descending.
Click the same header again to return to the original order.
On the phone, tap a header to sort a sheet.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop-hosted web: column header buttons titled 'Sort by <column>' in the spreadsheet preview (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:251-256).
Mobile: header buttons with sort arrows in the grid (TabularGridView.tsx:323-330).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not found.
prerequisites: A table, CSV or readable workbook open in the preview.
screens_and_controls: Header buttons with an up or down arrow showing direction.
Web header cells carry aria-sort ascending, descending or none (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:242-244).
journey: Click a third time: original order (tabular.ts:82-86).
feedback_and_outputs: Arrow icon on the sorted column.
Rows re-ordered; the file itself is not changed.

working: Numeric columns sort by value, text by locale-aware natural order, blanks last (tabular.ts:88-105).
Web header shows sort state to screen readers (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:242).
Mobile sort test covers numbers by value, then descending, then original order (TabularGridView.test.tsx:133).
incomplete: Sort applies only to the displayed first 500 rows after parsing; sorting is done on all parsed rows and then cut to 500 (SpreadsheetArtifact.tsx:90-93).
not_available: Filter by column: no code found.
Make table with header, banding and a name: managed-workbook-builder.ts writes no table part (lines 172-253).

Existing tables in an attached workbook are not shown as tables; the reader returns sheets as CSV (workbook-sheets.ts:682). Whether an edit keeps them is covered by the package-preserving edit path [inferred from managed-office-preservation.ts:1364].
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no sort or table found.

established.statement: A range can be turned into a structured table (header, banding, table name) in the workbook.
The user can sort and filter rows in a sheet by column.
S29.10 is listed among features the leaders do not offer and that are not built.

acceptance_criteria: Clicking a header sorts ascending; a second click sorts descending; a third restores the original order.
A column of 2, 10, 1 sorts as 1, 2, 10, not 1, 10, 2.
Empty cells stay at the bottom in both directions.
The header button has an accessible name that includes the column.
No filter control is present [current behaviour].
inferred: The brief's S29.10 'sort' half is met on web and mobile; 'filter' is not [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Update the brief so S29.10 shows sort done and filter not built.
[proposed] Write an Excel table or autofilter part only if the owner reverses the decision.

corrections.claim: implementation: missing / 'not built' on web, desktop, mobile; Status table 'In the code: not built'
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Sorting is built on web and mobile (shared SpreadsheetArtifact and mobile TabularGridView). The page's own prose and section 3 say so, so the frontmatter and Status table contradict the body.
corrections.correction: Web, desktop-hosted web and mobile: sort built (filter and table object not built). CLI, VS Code and Chrome: not built.

corrections.claim: Sort applies only to the displayed first 500 rows after parsing; sorting is done on all parsed rows and then cut to 500
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The sentence contradicts itself. The code sorts all rows, then slices to SPREADSHEET_ROW_CAP, so the sort is global. Rows past 500 are hidden but ordered. The same applies on mobile.
corrections.correction: Sort runs over all parsed rows, then only the first 500 sorted rows are shown, with a truncation notice. This is not a sort defect.

corrections.claim: Whether an edit keeps tables is covered by the package-preserving edit path [inferred from managed-office-preservation.ts:1364]
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Line 1364 is just the start of editManagedWorkbook. A test in the repo already shows an autoFilter element being preserved, so this can be stated as tested rather than unknown.
corrections.correction: The edit path keeps an existing autoFilter, per managed-office-preservation-markup.test.ts:1658,1800. Cite that, not line 1364. Table parts are unconfirmed.

corrections.claim: Acceptance 5: the header button has an accessible name that includes the column
corrections.what_the_code_shows: On web the name comes from the visible column text and a title. On mobile an explicit accessibilityLabel is set. The 'Sort by' wording is a title only.
corrections.correction: Say web exposes the column as the visible button text with a title tooltip; mobile sets an accessibilityLabel.

missing_facts: The frontmatter (implementation: missing, verification n/a, available_on empty) and the Status table say sorting is not built, but it ships on web and mobile through the shared SpreadsheetArtifact and TabularGridView (tabular.ts:80-106; ArtifactPreview.tsx:1946). Metadata consumers will read the wrong status.

The page says sort is shown on 'desktop-hosted web' but never checks the desktop app (apps/desktop/src) or the Chrome extension side panel. artifactPanel.ts:20 imports spreadsheetSafeExport from tabular, with no sort found there.

Existing autoFilter in an edited workbook is preserved by the managed edit path and has a test (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-preservation-markup.test.ts:1658,1800). The page lists this as unknown and says 'not tested by me'.
